sample_unit: patients (1861 radiographs) read by five readers
models_evaluated: four commercially available AI solutions for chest radiography (unnamed)

links.outcome: Reader diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in intended deployment mode
links.effect: AI assistance did not improve diagnostic accuracy; for pleural effusions and pulmonary nodules accuracy decreased in several reader-tool pairings due to increased false positives.
links.quote: AI assistance did not improve diagnostic accuracy.

links.outcome: Clinician performance with AI in the intended workflow versus without AI
links.effect: No improvement in diagnostic accuracy with AI; accuracy decreased in several reader-tool pairings for effusions and nodules through increased false positives.
links.quote: For pleural effusions and pulmonary nodules, accuracy decreased in several reader-tool pairings due to increased false positives.

unlisted_practices: Measuring AI effect on interpretation time, reader confidence, senior escalation and CT recommendation rates

screen.reason: Prospective multi-reader crossover study evaluating the impact of AI assistance versus unassisted reading on clinician diagnostic performance, workflow efficiency, confidence, and escalation rates.
